correctness.rationale: The original Pilaud–Poliakova arXiv full text Remark 61 explicitly gives the tight subset right-hand sides z_J=binom(|A|+|C|+1,2)+|B|; Prop.57 and Def.55 fix the standard affine realization sum x_i=binom(N+1,2). At m=1 write k=|J|, t=|A|+|C|, b=k-t. Then 2z_J=2k+t(t−1)≤k(k+1), since 0≤t≤k. At c=((N+1)/2)1, 2 slack ≥k(N−k); projected normal norm squared=k(N−k)/N, hence every valid tight hyperplane is at intrinsic distance at least sqrt(N*k*(N−k))/2 ≥sqrt(N(N−1))/2. The N singleton constraints are x_i≥1, so summing the N ball inequalities gives the opposite upper bound and equality forces every center coordinate equal. This proves both sharp radius and UNIQUE incenter for all n≥2. Independently enumerated ALL 2^N−2 subset right-hand sides for N=3..12, including singleton tangency. Finite test corroborates, not replaces the symbolic infinite proof.
